patient.name: Linda Petersen
patient.chiefComplaint: Altered mental status, husband reports "not acting right" since this morning

history.hpi: Husband states his wife has not been herself since this morning. He last saw her acting normally around 7:00 AM when she took her morning insulin injection. He found her slumped in a kitchen chair at approximately 9:45 AM, sweaty, and slurring her words when he tried to talk to her. She skipped breakfast because she got a phone call. An insulin pen and a used glucose test strip wrapper are on the kitchen table next to her.
history.lastOralIntake: Black coffee around 7:30 AM; skipped breakfast
history.events: Took morning insulin as usual around 7:00 AM per husband, then skipped breakfast due to a phone call. Husband found her slumped at the kitchen table around 9:45 AM, diaphoretic and slurring her speech, and called 911.

scene.dispatch: Respond for a 54-year-old female, altered mental status, husband on scene
scene.location: Single-family home, kitchen; patient seated in a kitchen chair at the table
scene.safety: Scene appears safe; husband is cooperative and calm; no hazards or weapons noted
scene.bystanders: Husband present at bedside; states his wife has not been acting right since this morning and has been a type 2 diabetic on insulin for 10 years
visualCues: Insulin pen and used glucose test strip wrapper on the kitchen table
Patient's shirt visibly damp with sweat
Half-empty cup of coffee on the table
Patient slouched in chair, slow to respond when husband says her name

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 54-year-old female seated at the kitchen table, diaphoretic, with slurred speech and a slowed response to voice. Husband is present and provides history of insulin use and a skipped breakfast.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent, able to swallow and manage secretions, no stridor
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, strong and rapid; skin diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.pupils: Equal, round, reactive to light bilaterally
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Moves all extremities spontaneously, no focal weakness noted, mild generalized tremor

expectedActions.shortAction: Primary survey; ensure airway remains patent, reposition as needed
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Airway: Make sure airway remains patent; reposition patient as needed
expectedActions.rationale: Rule out airway compromise before further assessment

expectedActions.shortAction: Assess AVPU and Glasgow Coma Score
expectedActions.rationale: Establishes baseline mental status for trending
Insulin pen on scene and AMS make hypoglycemia a leading differential

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform validated stroke scale (facial droop, arm drift, speech)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Facial smile/grimace – ask patient to smile Arm drift – close eyes and hold out arms for count of 10 seconds Speech – ask patient to say "You can't teach an old dog new tricks"
expectedActions.rationale: Slurred speech requires a formal stroke scale to screen for a stroke mimic

expectedActions.shortAction: Obtain SAMPLE history and last known well time from husband
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: History – "last known well" and source of that information
expectedActions.rationale: Onset time is essential if stroke cannot be excluded

expectedActions.shortAction: Administer oral glucose gel 25 g PO (BGL 42 mg/dL, patient able to swallow)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Conscious patient with a patent airway: Glucose, oral (in form of glucose tablets, glucose gel, tube of cake icing, etc.) Adult Dosing: 25 g
expectedActions.rationale: Symptomatic hypoglycemia (BGL <60 mg/dL) with a patent airway meets criteria for oral glucose

transitions.condition: Crew recognizes hypoglycemia (BGL 42 mg/dL) with intact airway and administers 25 g oral glucose promptly
Crew fails to check blood glucose or delays oral glucose administration; patient's mental status continues to decline

phases.name: Oral glucose given
phases.description: After 25 g of oral glucose, the patient's speech clears and she becomes oriented. Husband confirms this is consistent with prior low blood sugar episodes.
phases.triggerCondition: Oral glucose was administered promptly after BGL 42 mg/dL was identified; symptomatic hypoglycemia responds to glucose within several minutes.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses strong and regular; skin drying
clinicalPresentation.pupils: Equal, round, reactive to light bilaterally
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Moves all extremities equally, no focal weakness, tremor resolved
otherFindings: Oriented to person, place, time, and event
No facial droop or arm drift
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Sorry about that, I get that way sometimes when my sugar drops. I forgot to eat breakfast."

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vital signs and mental status after glucose administration
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Reassess vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment) and mental status
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms response to treatment and rules out need for repeat dosing

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport to hospital; not all safe-release criteria are met
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If symptoms of hypoglycemia resolve after treatment, release without transport should only be considered if all the following are true
expectedActions.rationale: A single skipped meal alone does not satisfy all documented release-at-scene criteria; transport for evaluation is indicated

transitions.condition: Crew elects to transport the now-alert patient to the closest appropriate receiving facility for further evaluation

phases.name: Transport initiated
phases.description: Patient is packaged and transported, remaining alert and oriented with stable vital signs en route.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew initiated transport after the patient's mental status normalized following oral glucose administration.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses strong and regular; skin warm and dry
clinicalPresentation.pupils: Equal, round, reactive to light bilaterally
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Moves all extremities equally, no focal deficit
otherFindings: Asking about missing her morning insulin dosing schedule
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel back to normal now, thank you."

expectedActions.shortAction: Continue reassessment of mental status and vitals en route to prevent complications
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Protect patient from complications of altered mental status (e.g., respiratory failure, shock, cardiopulmonary arrest)
expectedActions.rationale: Ongoing monitoring guards against recurrence or unrecognized deterioration

phases.name: Oral glucose delayed
phases.description: With glucose unchecked or oral glucose withheld, the patient's mental status continues to deteriorate. She is now unresponsive and unable to protect her own airway.
phases.triggerCondition: Blood glucose was not checked promptly, or oral glucose was withheld, while untreated hypoglycemia progressed to unresponsiveness.

clinicalPresentation.airway: At risk; not purposefully protecting airway, occasional soft snoring respirations
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses weak and rapid; skin profoundly diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Withdraws to painful stimuli only, no purposeful movement

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize patient can no longer safely receive oral glucose
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Unconscious patient, or patients who are unable to protect their own airway:
expectedActions.rationale: Oral glucose in an unresponsive patient risks aspiration; this is outside oral glucose criteria

expectedActions.shortAction: Position patient for airway protection; apply high-flow oxygen
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: With depressed mental status, initial focus is on airway protection, oxygenation, ventilation, and perfusion
expectedActions.rationale: Airway protection takes priority once the patient can no longer manage secretions purposefully

expectedActions.shortAction: Initiate immediate transport to closest appropriate receiving facility
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Initiate transport to closest appropriate receiving facility for further treatment of refractory hypoglycemia
expectedActions.rationale: Definitive treatment (IV dextrose/glucagon) is beyond BLS scope; rapid transport is the priority intervention
